newsitem.title: USA: AOL sets program, to hold members at 8 mln.
newsitem.headline: AOL sets program, to hold members at 8 mln.

text.p: America Online Inc said that it agreed to offer customer refunds or credits to its members experiencing problems and that it plans to hold membership at eight million for the short term until it can handle increased demand for its service.
The largest online service said that it is offering a series of options as part of its recent discussions with the attorneys general in about 35 states.
AOL said that AOL members who feel they have not received sufficient value due to busy signals can receive a credit of one month's membership fee.
AOL said that it will accept cancellations by U.S. mail and by fax, in addition to telephone, in an answer to some members complaints that they cannot cancel the service.

The company also said that it is on track with its program to upgrade its network by 75 percent to improve connectivity for members by adding 200,000-plus modems. It said that it expects to be able to handle more than 16 million member sessions daily by the end of June.
AOL said it has added more than 150,000 modems over the past year and that it will soon break ground on its third data center, a 180,000 square foot facility.

AOL said in a statement that was issued after comments made by attorneys general in the states of Connecticuit, Illinois and New York that its first priority is to serve its existing members before adding new members and to work around the clock to expand its system capacity as quickly as possibility.
AOL said that it plans to have a formal agreement with the attorneys general in dozens of states shortly.

"Over the past week, we have been in discussions with Attorneys General to convey to them our commitment to fully satisfy their concerns about the access issue," said AOL CEO Steve Case, in a statement.

"We have discussed with them the actions we were planning to take to ensure the complete satisfaction of our members, which is of paramount importance," Case said. "We are continuing to work with them and expect to have a formal agreement shortly."
AOL said it has begun to bring on additional 600 customer support representatives, to bring the total to 4,500 by June. Customer service is 75 percent of its total workforce.
AOL also said that it agreed to a transitional period during which it will indicate that its service is subject to availabilty during peak periods.
